headline: NSB briefing Thu Oct 22) -- Taiwan says China spread 2.5M+ false items in 9 months, up 48%, ahead of Nov 28 local elections
dek: Taiwan's National Security Bureau told lawmakers China spread more than 2.5 million pieces of disputed or false online information in the first nine months of 2026, up about 48% from 1.69 million a year earlier, targeting energy, food security, defence policy and specific candidates ahead of the…
sources: Taiwan National Security Bureau briefing to lawmakers, Oct 22, 2026 (Director-General Tsai Ming-yen)
fault_line: Election interference documented -- or Taipei's pre-election framing? Beijing denies; prosecutors get the evidence before Nov 28.

sections.what_happened: Taiwan's National Security Bureau told lawmakers China spread more than 2.5 million pieces of disputed or false online information in the first nine months of 2026, up about 48% from 1.69 million a year earlier, targeting energy, food security, defence policy and specific candidates ahead of the Nov 28 local elections, using AI-generated videos, fake accounts and coordinated comment flooding. NSB Director-General Tsai Ming-yen said Beijing is mobilising airlines to offer discounted tickets to Taiwanese in China who return to vote for Chinese-backed candidates and is believed to be providing illicit funding to candidates; government networks face about 2.58 million intrusion attempts daily; the NSB hopes to give evidence to prosecutors before the Nov 28 vote. China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to a request for comment; Beijing has previously denied interfering in Taiwan's elections.
sections.what_verified: Reuters, Focus Taiwan/Taipei Times and ANI converge on the NSB briefing figures.
sections.what_disputed: Beijing has previously denied interfering in Taiwan's elections and its Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond on this briefing; the NSB figures are Taiwan-government counts, not independently audited.
sections.why_matters: Taipei says Beijing flooded the island with 2.5 million fake posts before the vote -- and is now offering cheap flights home to vote the 'right' way.
